top3_directives: Collapse 'THE OCEAN?' into the main title as one styled line or animate it in as a beat — a static second text block reads as two competing systems and caps the score

Strengthen the focal point: the character is small and pushed to the corner with its glow clipped — scale it up ~25% and ensure the rim-light and shadow don't get cut by the rock silhouette
Fill the large empty sky dead zone (top 40% is nearly bare) — push the sun/rays larger or move the character/text up to compress vertical dead space
Add a subtle drop shadow or outline to 'NOPE.' so it separates from the flat blue gradient instead of floating in it
Strengthen the eye path: the sun rays point down-left away from the character — re-angle beams so they lead toward the figure and the text
Move the title card down or enlarge the character — the top third and the stripe band leave a wide low-interest middle zone
Give the character a stronger ground shadow / rim light so it pops off the flat dune background at a glance
Unify the odd horizontal stripe band behind the dunes — it reads as an unexplained artifact rather than intentional design
Fill the large empty blue sky mid-band (upper-left quadrant is a dead zone) with a subtle secondary element — a distant cloud, bird, or gradient shift — to guide the eye from character to caption

Give the 'SAME BLUE.' pill stronger separation from the blue sky — a soft drop shadow or warmer stroke would prevent the dark-navy badge from blending into the background at a glance

The incoming light beam visually terminates at the panel's top edge instead of passing coherently into the refractive element — extend/blend the beam so the entry point reads as continuous physics, not a layering error
The 'AIR' label is the only text and carries all context — give it slightly more presence (weight or size) so the concept lands instantly at thumb-scroll speed, or add a minimal action verb

Bottom third and lower-right of the panel are dead zones — either raise the character to overlap the panel edge for depth, or add a subtle refracted-ray hint exiting bottom-right to complete the eye path sun → scatter → exit → character
Fill the dead lower-right quadrant — the mascot is isolated bottom-left with nothing balancing the frame; shift the diagram panel down or add a secondary visual anchor

Clarify the collision cluster — the overlapping light-blue circles where the rays meet read as mush at phone size; simplify to one bright impact flash with a single scatter burst

Boost the sky-lamp separation: the pale translucent lamps nearly dissolve into the blue background — add a stronger drop shadow, rim stroke, or warm glow (they're lamps, after all) so the pattern reads as a subject, not mush

Give the character a floor/scene anchor — it floats in empty blue with a huge dead zone between the lamp field and its feet; crop the lamp cluster lower or add ground context to compress the composition
Replace the flat navy pill caption with a treatment tied to the palette (warm accent or glowing text) — currently it's the only high-contrast element but visually disconnected from the scene's style
Fill the large empty gradient dead zones (top-left sky and entire bottom-right quadrant) — shift the card panel up-center and let the character occupy the lower-right to balance the frame
Unify the two card label placements: DEEP sits mid-card while WASHED sits lower next to the sun icon, creating uneven eye path — align both headers to identical vertical positions
The character's pointing gesture aims at nothing; redirect the pose toward the card panel or the sun to connect figure and focal content

Remove or reposition the red strike-through so it doesn't cross through the letters of 'NOT A MIRROR' — it currently damages legibility of the only text element; strike beside the label or underline instead
Enlarge the character ~30-40% and shift the UFO beam to connect toward him — right now the beam's pool and the character are visually unrelated, weakening the eye path and the joke
Fill the top-left/bottom-right dead zones subtly (gradient vignette, faint cloud/ground texture) so the vertical frame doesn't feel empty above and below the action
Fill the large empty upper region of the blue panel — nearly 40% dead space kills depth; add a subtle sky-through-glass gradient or faint grid
Strengthen the caption pill's edge contrast — the translucent dark pill over mid-blue sky is a bit mushy in daylight; add a tighter dark stroke or stronger shadow
Make the X/check outcome marks more immediate focal anchors — they sit low-contrast against the panel; bump saturation or add a subtle glow so the win/lose state reads instantly
Fill the large empty gradient band between the headline and the character — the middle third is a dead zone that lets the eye drift off-frame
Create one dominant focal point: either enlarge the character or move the headline closer so text and subject read as a single composition instead of two separated anchors
Add a subtle glow or rim-light contrast behind 'THEY JUST MATCHED.' so the white type pops harder on the mid-blue sky in daylight viewing
